analysis.overall: You spent 82% of your day in range with a very stable morning, though late-night digestion and a delayed surge after breakfast drove a couple of stubborn highs.

events.title: Evening snack bump
events.description: A 10g snack caused a brief rise up to 183 mg/dL, but a quick correction brought you smoothly back into range within two hours.

events.title: Late-night stubborn high
events.description: Carbs from your late meal kicked in overnight, sending glucose to a peak of 223 mg/dL around 2:00 AM despite several small correction boluses.

events.title: Smooth morning low-tide
events.description: Fasting glucose gently coasted down to a low of 79 mg/dL without triggering a sharp crash.

events.title: Breakfast pre-bolus success
events.description: Your 3.8u dose for 50g of carbs initially kept your readings flat between 90 and 124 mg/dL through the morning.

events.title: Delayed afternoon spike
events.description: Delayed digestion from breakfast caused a sudden rise up to 255 mg/dL, though stacked corrections started pulling it back down quickly.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Keep an eye on larger morning meals—even if glucose stays flat for the first two hours, delayed digestion can cause a rise early in the afternoon.
